2026-08.title: August 2026 — Neil Rose times it perfectly
2026-08.body_html:
Morning all,

Two gameweeks gone and August already has a moral: the chip is only as good as the week you play it.

Neil Rose has won the month, and he did it from nowhere. Fifty-five points in Gameweek 1 left him 13th of 39 and completely anonymous. Then he emptied the tank in Gameweek 2 — Bench Boost on, Bruno Fernandes with the armband — and came back with 147. Nobody else in the league broke 130 in a single week all month. Final August total: 202, sixteen clear of Shannon Engelbrecht, and an overall rank that went from 2.9 million to 5,501 in seven days.

Ten of us played a Bench Boost in August, five in each gameweek. The five who went early — Shannon, Steve Darbin, Liam Addis, Bobby Cole and Lee Chadwick — used it in the week the global average was 50. The five who waited until GW2 used it in the week the average was 81. Shannon's boost returned 82. Neil's returned 147. Same chip, one week apart, a 65-point gap. Chips are timing, and timing is mostly luck, but let's all agree it was genius.

The armband was the other fork in the road. In GW1 twenty-six managers captained Haaland for a doubled two, which was democratic if nothing else. In GW2 twenty stayed loyal to Haaland (26 points) while sixteen switched to Bruno (46). That twenty-point swing is roughly the whole month.

The title race. Two gameweeks is not a season, but Kyle Davies deserves a mention: 26th after GW1 on 46 points, then 126 in GW2, and he's now 5th without spending a chip. Nick Holt has come from 21st to 6th. Going the other way, Bobby Cole was 3rd after GW1 and is now 11th.

HALL OF FAME

Kyle Davies' starting XI has produced 12 goals, more than anyone, and he's tied with Neil Rose on 23 bonus points. Bobby Cole leads the assists on 11, ahead of Steve Darbin, Nick Male, Karim Ali and Daniel Rose on 9.

By position it splits neatly. Shannon Engelbrecht's midfield has racked up 83 points — the best engine room in the league by some distance, with Kyle Davies on 75 and Alex Preston on 72. Neil Rose has the best defence on 56, then Steve Darbin and Karim Ali on 49. Up top, Andrew Cook and Sean Wren lead on 45 apiece. Liam Addis has the most productive goalkeeper on 14.

Neil Rose is also joint-top on defensive contributions with 8, alongside Murali Lambotharan, Harry Chapman and Flannery Devine Gibbons. Credit too to the differential hunters: Neil owns Egan of Hull and nobody else does (9 points), while Gary Bartlett was alone on Cherki for 14.

HALL OF SHAME

Zach Mettee handed the captaincy to Thiago in GW1. Thiago scored nothing, so Zach got nothing. Undeterred, Zach captained Thiago again in GW2 and got four. Four captain points for the month. Neil Rose has 50. Zach has gone from 11th to 32nd and we are all quietly rooting for him.

The bench was the real graveyard. Neil Macdougall has left 33 points sitting down, 22 of them in GW1 alone. Daniel Rose left 28 there and George Dallman 24. But the painful ones are at the top: Steve Darbin benched 21 points in GW2 and lost the month by 17, and Shannon Engelbrecht benched 20 and lost it by 16. Both of them had Manager of the Month on the bench, watching.

Tom Stuffins took 8 points of hits and finished joint-19th; his gross score would have put him 15th. Trent Torrence and Harry Chapman each set 4 points on fire. Gavin Berwitz's squad has collected five yellow cards in two weeks, a league high. And spare a thought for Stuart Gibbons, who scored 40 in a week when the average was 81 and props up the table on 94.
